title: Kilimanjaro National Park Guide | Climb & Trek | Tanzania Safari Magic
h1: Kilimanjaro National Park — Climb Africa’s Highest Peak
meta_description: Climb Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) with Tanzania Safari Magic. UNESCO park, Machame, Lemosho & Marangu routes, best time, costs, and safari + trek combos from Arusha. Free quote.

faqs.a: Uhuru Peak on Kibo stands at 5,895 metres (19,341 ft) — the highest point in Africa and the world’s tallest free-standing mountain. Kilimanjaro National Park protects the summit and surrounding montane forest.

faqs.q: Is Kilimanjaro a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
faqs.a: Yes. UNESCO inscribed Kilimanjaro National Park in 1987 (criterion vii) for its outstanding volcanic form, snow-capped peak, and isolation above the savannah. The park covers roughly 75,575 ha after forest extensions.

faqs.q: Do I need technical climbing experience?
faqs.a: No ropes or mountaineering skills are required on standard trekking routes — Kilimanjaro is often called “Everyman’s Everest.” Fitness, slow acclimatization, and a licensed guide (mandatory under TANAPA rules) matter far more than technical climbing ability.

faqs.q: What is the best time to climb Kilimanjaro?
faqs.a: Peak dry windows are January–mid-March and June–October. January–February often has clearer summit views; July–September is busiest. April–May long rains and November short rains mean muddier trails and fewer climbers.

Machame (6–7 days) is the most popular scenic “Whiskey” route. Lemosho / Northern Circuit (7–9 days) offer better acclimatization and quieter trails. Marangu (5–6 days) has hut accommodation. Umbwe is steeper and for fit, experienced trekkers.

faqs.q: Can I combine Kilimanjaro with a safari?
faqs.a: Yes — and many guests do. Trek Kilimanjaro first (or after), then add Serengeti, Ngorongoro, Tarangire, or a Zanzibar beach extension. Ask Tanzania Safari Magic in Arusha for a private climb + safari itinerary.

faqs.q: Where is the park and how do I get there from Arusha?
faqs.a: Kilimanjaro National Park is in Kilimanjaro Region near Moshi, about 300 km south of the equator. Park HQ is at Marangu (~44 km from Moshi, ~86 km from Kilimanjaro International Airport). We arrange transfers from Arusha or JRO.
